discussion_comments.comment_body: **Should-fix — this test does not exercise blob extraction.** It sets a temporary blob directory but calls only `stripInjectedMemoryTags()` and `scrubLiveCredentials()`; it never invokes `sanitizeContent()` with extractable content or reads a stored blob. A regression that writes a live token into a blob would still pass. Exercise the sanitizer/storage boundary and assert the resulting bytes contain no credential.

**should-fix**: `getEmbeddingCacheStateForTests` puts a test-only accessor on the production module surface, and exporting `vectorSimilarities` only serves the new test. The test can check behavior instead: run recall again after an `UPDATE`/`DELETE` and assert the scores, without reading cache internals or counting `JSON.parse` calls.

**should-fix**: `Parameters<typeof JSON.parse>[1]` is a type hack the repo bans (AGENTS.md: no `ReturnType<>`/`Parameters<>`). Better to drop the `JSON.parse` spy altogether and assert recall results after mutating rows; see the comment on `getEmbeddingCacheStateForTests`.

**should-fix**: this test only checks that the index names exist in `sqlite_master`, which restates the DDL. It would still pass if the planner never uses the indexes (and for `idx_edges_type_source_target` it doesn't). The repo's testing rules count this as a static echo; please delete it. The `ingestMemory` test at lines 89–106 is similar: it asserts `m1.memoryId === "mem_1"` and one linked neighbor, which existing tests in `proactive-linking.test.ts` already cover.

**should-fix** — hand-swapping `limits.markReached` with an `as typeof limits.markReached` cast breaks the repo's no-`as` rule and leaks the stub if anything between assignment and `try` throws. `vi.spyOn(limits, "markReached").mockResolvedValue({ switched: false })` plus `vi.restoreAllMocks()` is the sanctioned seam. Also, the change rewires `baseUrl` and `modelId` too, but the test only records the provider; asserting `toHaveBeenCalledWith("openai-codex", expect.any(String), expect.objectContaining({ modelId: codex.id, baseUrl: codex.baseUrl }))` covers the whole attribution.

**should-fix:** This test only checks that `addMessageToChat` appends a bash component, not the >100-line replay behavior the PR fixes. The preceding test already exercises that path and asserts its visible output; remove this wiring-only duplicate. The empty-result case in `packages/tui/test/bash-execution-replay.test.ts:136` likewise asserts an unchanged empty value/no count rather than the claimed absence of an output pane.

Fixed: the object-existence-only test is gone — `packages/coding-agent/test/bash-replay-seeding.test.ts` now asserts the RENDERED output of the >100-line replay, and the empty-result case in `packages/tui/test/bash-execution-replay.test.ts` ("emits no output pane for an empty recorded result") asserts the ABSENCE of an output pane (three rows: the borders and the command header) instead of an unchanged empty value.

**should-fix — test contract:** This only checks that the options object lacks `fetchDynamicModels`; it never proves the consumer-visible keyless behavior (the authored seed stays available and no remote roster replaces it). Repository testing rules disallow field-wiring assertions. Exercise the model manager's resolved catalog, or remove this test if that behavior is already covered.

Replaced in 1981cfc1e with a resolveProviderModels test: without a key the committed seed (deepseek-v4-pro-0813) is the resolved catalog, and with a key the live roster replaces it.

_🤖 Addressed by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_

Fixed: the source-text assertions are replaced by behavioural coverage - the test drives every exposed extension context and asserts the observable outcome (the promise resolves and `onError` fires exactly once), instead of grepping the implementation files.

**nit** — `missing`, `null`, `non-numeric`, `non-finite`, `boolean`, and `object` all go through the same branch: `toNumber()` returns `undefined` (`utils.ts:13-24`). Only `zero`/`negative` (the `> 0` check) and `fractional` (the integer guard) reach different code. Per the repo testing rules, parameterized rows should each cover a distinct branch. One `undefined`-path row plus `zero` and `fractional` would cover the same ground.
Trimmed in da11942d7a to `non-numeric` (the `toNumber` undefined path) and `zero` (the `> 0` check). `fractional` is no longer invalid now that both branches share `toPositiveNumber`.

**blocking (convention)** — `checkModelRequestOwnership` (2979-line `test/helpers/model-request-ownership.ts`) parses implementation source text and asserts on it, and requires a `// model-request: <owner> — <why>` comment above ~475 sites across 12 packages. AGENTS.md explicitly bans this: *"Never source-grep. A test that reads an implementation file and asserts on its text … is banned … enforce structural invariants … with a type test or an oxlint rule — never a string scan of the source."* The PR body concedes the limit (string-concatenated `authorization` header, swallowed `catch`, typed-parameter sessions all pass). It also makes every future `fetch`/`WebSocket`/`Bun.connect` anywhere in the repo (scripts, benches, `omptype`, `stats`, `tui/scripts`) fail CI until annotated — a repo-wide contributor tax that needs maintainer buy-in. Suggest dropping the checker, its self-test, and the annotation comments from this PR; if the invariant is wanted, propose it as an oxlint rule separately.

**should-fix** — this test only exercises the single-turn `runSubprocess` path and asserts the reason string contains `task.maxSessionRuntimeMs=1`. It does not defend the PR's actual contract — that the budget is cumulative and survives parked/resumed follow-up turns. As written it passes even though a resumed turn restarts the clock and `runSubagentFollowUpTurn` never receives the cap (see executor.ts finding). A meaningful test would run turn 1, then a follow-up turn, and assert total elapsed runtime is bounded across both.
Fixed: the regression now runs turn 1, waits past the cap, then drives a follow-up turn and asserts the follow-up aborts with `task.maxSessionRuntimeMs`.

**should-fix (test doesn't defend the real contract):** the "routes wakeup completion to the registered owning session" test registers a fake child session `{ yieldQueue: { enqueue: childEnqueue } }`, which trivially accepts any `enqueue("async-result", …)` call. The real `YieldQueue` only accepts a kind after `register()`, and that registration is skipped for non-owning (subagent) sessions (`sdk.ts:2994` is gated on the top-level `asyncJobManager`). So this test passes while a real subagent-owned wakeup would be dropped (see the `sdk.ts:1603` finding). Consider asserting against a real subagent session's `yieldQueue` — or an assertion that the routed delivery actually reaches the agent loop — so this path is genuinely covered.

should-fix: this test doesn't exercise the code the PR adds. The assertion depends only on the `{ "compaction.thresholdTokens": 64_000 }` override you pass directly into `createSubagentSettings`; the `task.childContextBudgetTokens: 64_000` in the base settings is unused, and `createSubagentSettings` simply spreads overrides onto the snapshot. So this passes even if the entire `executor.ts` change is reverted — it proves override passthrough, not the new behavior.

The actual contract (reading `task.childContextBudgetTokens`, `Math.max(0, Math.trunc(...))`, the `>0` gate, and mapping it to `compaction.thresholdTokens`) lives in `runSubprocess` and is untested. Per AGENTS.md testing guidance this is a tautology asserting field wiring rather than downstream behavior. Consider extracting the budget→override computation into a small pure helper and asserting: 0/negative/fractional inputs disable or truncate, and a positive budget produces the threshold override.

Fixed. The budget policy now runs inside `createSubagentSettings`, and the tests exercise that production path without manually supplying the expected threshold. Coverage includes disabled zero/negative values, fractional truncation, and both inherited-threshold precedence cases.
Nit: asserts wiring, not contract — `requests.toHaveLength(1)` + terminal state already prove no rewrite. Drop the `saveArtifact` spy.

**should-fix:** `undefined as unknown as Model` bypasses the `Agent.setModel(Model)` contract to manufacture the no-model branch, contrary to the repo's no-type-hacks rule. Exercise the missing-model state through a supported session/model-selection setup instead; this assertion makes the regression fixture depend on an invalid setter call.
